title: Summary Of The Lesson From The Cosmos There Is No God But Allah

questions.question: What big idea is seen among the things in the world in this passage?
questions.answer: They help one another.

questions.question: What are living things trying to keep?
questions.answer: Their being alive and their work.

questions.question: Why is this helping one another amazing?
questions.answer: It is more than those things can do by themselves.

questions.question: Which comes to help plants?
questions.answer: The clouds.

questions.question: Which group helps animals get what they need?
questions.answer: Plants.

questions.question: Which group helps people?
questions.answer: Animals.

questions.question: What example shows care for a baby?
questions.answer: Milk is given to feed the baby.

questions.question: From where do living things sometimes get food and needs?
questions.answer: From places they do not expect.

questions.question: What happens to food inside the body?
questions.answer: Tiny bits of it are sent to the body’s cells.

questions.question: What do these examples show about the Lord of all worlds?
questions.answer: He cares for everything and rules everything with mercy.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the way the universe is managed?
questions.answer: Like a well-run palace.

questions.question: Why can lifeless things not be helping each other on their own?
questions.answer: Because they have no feeling or mind by themselves.

questions.question: Then who makes them help each other?
questions.answer: The Merciful, Wise, and Glorious Sustainer.

questions.question: Name two other big signs in the passage besides co-operation.
questions.answer: Balance and protection.

questions.question: What is one example of beauty in creation named here?
questions.answer: The sky, the earth, and flowers are made beautiful.

questions.question: What does this whole teamwork, balance, beauty, and order do?
questions.answer: It gives a strong witness to Allah.

questions.question: What truth does the passage say we can notice in the world?
questions.answer: A truth of working together.

questions.question: When changes keep happening in the world, what do beings still try to do?
questions.answer: They try to keep existing, stay alive, and do their jobs.

questions.question: Does this teamwork stay inside their own power, or go beyond it?
questions.answer: It goes beyond their own power.

questions.question: What helps the plant world according to the passage?
questions.answer: The clouds help it.

questions.question: What helps the human world in the examples given?
questions.answer: The animal world helps it.

questions.question: What feeds the little baby?
questions.answer: Milk.

questions.question: Why is the giving of needs to living things a sign?
questions.answer: Because they receive what they need in ways they could not arrange themselves.

questions.question: Who controls the food particles that go to body cells?
questions.answer: Their Lord controls them.

questions.question: What do these examples teach about the One who cares for the world?
questions.answer: He is caring and in charge of all things.

questions.question: What picture is used to help us imagine the universe?
questions.answer: A palace.

questions.question: How do lifeless things act in this passage?
questions.answer: They act as if they are helping carefully and knowingly.

questions.question: What does that tell us?
questions.answer: Someone powerful and wise makes them do that.

questions.question: What kind of regularity is seen from planets down to body parts?
questions.answer: Great balance and guarding.

questions.question: What small things are named to show order in tiny places?
questions.answer: Corn and pomegranates.

questions.question: Which creatures are named to show that jobs are given to all kinds of things?
questions.answer: Even honey-bees.

questions.question: Why is this called the second wing of the world’s testimony?
questions.answer: Because it is another big way creation points to Allah.

questions.question: What do many beings in the passage do with each other?
questions.answer: They support each other.

questions.question: What are animate beings trying to protect besides existence?
questions.answer: Their life.

questions.question: What else are they trying to carry out?
questions.answer: Their duties.

questions.question: Why can this not be only their own doing?
questions.answer: Because the help and order are too great for them alone.

questions.question: What comes quickly to help living creatures first in the examples?
questions.answer: The elements.

questions.question: After that, what helps plants grow?
questions.answer: The clouds.

questions.question: After plants are helped, whom do plants help?
questions.answer: Animals.

questions.question: After animals are helped, whom do animals help?
questions.answer: Human beings.

questions.question: What surprising thing happens with sustenance for living things?
questions.answer: It comes from places they did not expect.

questions.question: What happens to the body’s cells?
questions.answer: They receive food particles.

questions.question: What does all this prove about the Sustainer?
questions.answer: He rules all with mercy and care.

questions.question: Why does the passage say unfeeling things need a ruler over them?
questions.answer: Because they still act together in a careful way.

questions.question: What qualities does the Sustainer have here?
questions.answer: He is compassionate, wise, and glorious.

questions.question: What great patterns are seen everywhere in the cosmos?
questions.answer: Teamwork, balance, protection, beauty, order, and assigned jobs.

questions.question: What is the main lesson from all these patterns?
questions.answer: The whole creation is giving witness to Allah.

questions.question: In this passage, what do the beings in the world do while many changes happen around them?
questions.answer: They keep going and help one another.

questions.question: What does the passage say this teamwork is greater than?
questions.answer: Greater than their own ability.

questions.question: Give one example of something in nature helping something else.
questions.answer: Clouds help plants.

questions.question: How do plants help the next group after them?
questions.answer: They help feed animals.

questions.question: How do animals help people?
questions.answer: They provide help and benefit for humans.

questions.question: What is one special gift for babies named in the passage?
questions.answer: Milk.

questions.question: What makes the giving of food to creatures so wonderful?
questions.answer: They get it without being able to make all of it happen themselves.

questions.question: What does this tell us about how Allah cares for creation?
questions.answer: He gives what is needed with mercy.

questions.question: What building is used as an example for how the cosmos is run?
questions.answer: A palace.

questions.question: Are hard, lifeless things aware by themselves?
questions.answer: No, they are not aware by themselves.

questions.question: Then how do they still seem to help in careful ways?
questions.answer: Allah makes them serve by His command.

questions.question: What is seen from huge planets down to tiny body parts?
questions.answer: Careful balance and protection.

questions.question: Where can we see beauty mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: In the sky, the earth, and flowers.

questions.question: What are two examples showing that jobs are given in creation?
questions.answer: The sun and moon, and also bees.

questions.question: Put the main message in one short sentence.
questions.answer: Everything works together in an ordered way that points to Allah.

questions.question: What truth about the world is spoken about first in this passage?
questions.answer: The truth that creation works together.

questions.question: What are living beings trying to do during constant changes?
questions.answer: Stay alive and do their tasks.

questions.question: What does the passage help us understand about their power?
questions.answer: Their own power is not enough for all this.

questions.question: What helps the world of plants from above?
questions.answer: Clouds do.

questions.question: Which kingdom helps the human kingdom in the examples?
questions.answer: The animal kingdom.

questions.question: What food is specially mentioned for infants?
questions.answer: Milk.

questions.question: What is surprising about how creatures receive provision?
questions.answer: It comes to them from unexpected places.

questions.question: What small parts of the body are spoken about?
questions.answer: Cells.

questions.question: What reaches those cells?
questions.answer: Food particles.

questions.question: What do these acts of care show about the Lord of the worlds?
questions.answer: He is merciful and takes care of all.

questions.question: Why is the teamwork of lifeless things an important clue?
questions.answer: Because lifeless things cannot plan that help on their own.

questions.question: Who, then, sends them to help each other?
questions.answer: A compassionate and wise Sustainer.

questions.question: What two big ideas are joined with co-operation later in the passage?
questions.answer: Balance and preservation.

questions.question: What examples show order in both big and small things?
questions.answer: From star systems to fruits.

questions.question: What tiny worker is named at the end of the list of duties?
questions.answer: The honey-bee.

questions.question: What does the passage say these great truths become?
questions.answer: They become the second wing of creation’s witness.

questions.question: What can we see happening among the beings in the world?
questions.answer: They assist one another.

questions.question: What are animate beings trying to maintain?
questions.answer: Their existence, their life, and their duties.

questions.question: What does the passage say about their own strength compared with this work?
questions.answer: This work is beyond their own strength.

questions.question: Name the order of help in the examples from nature.
questions.answer: Elements help living things, clouds help plants, plants help animals, and animals help people.

questions.question: What example shows gentle care for a very young child?
questions.answer: Nourishment is provided for the baby.

questions.question: Why is that a sign of mercy?
questions.answer: Because the baby cannot get it by itself.

questions.question: What is another sign of care for living things besides milk?
questions.answer: Their food comes from places they did not expect.

questions.question: What happens inside the body with food?
questions.answer: It is carried to the cells.

questions.question: Who is said to employ these tiny particles?
questions.answer: Their Sustainer.

questions.question: What do all these examples prove about the One who runs the universe?
questions.answer: He is merciful, caring, and in control.

questions.question: What is strange about solid, lifeless things in this passage?
questions.answer: They still act together in a careful way.

questions.question: What must be true if lifeless things act like that?
questions.answer: A wise and glorious Lord is directing them.

questions.question: What is seen everywhere from the largest things to the smallest?
questions.answer: Harmony, balance, and safekeeping.

questions.question: What places show beauty in creation here?
questions.answer: The heavens, the earth, and flowers.

questions.question: What does giving duties to everything show?
questions.answer: That creation is arranged on purpose.

questions.question: What final idea should a student learn from this passage?
questions.answer: The ordered help in all creation points to Allah.
